newsitem.title: FRANCE: French presidency denies plan to reshuffle cabinet.
newsitem.headline: French presidency denies plan to reshuffle cabinet.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac has no plans to reshuffle his cabinet to pick up political momentum ahead of 1998 general elections, a spokeswoman said on Monday, denying a newspaper report that changes were in the works.
"A reshuffle is not topical and has no basis. These rumours are just pure speculation," presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said.

The left-wing daily Liberation said that Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe, whose approval ratings are near record lows while unemployment is at a record 12.7 percent, were weighing a reshuffle of the centre-right cabinet in February.
"We must do it while there is still wind in our sails," an anonymous source close to the president was quoted as saying.
Senior Chirac aide Dominique Villepin favoured a rejigging that was "as broad as possible," the newspaper added.

Faced with growing voter unrest over rising unemployment and a government austerity programme aimed at helping France qualify for a single European currency from 1999, Chirac and Juppe have repeatedly denied plans for a shake-up in recent months.

Juppe said recently he intended to remain prime minister until after the general elections and has launched a charm offensive to brush up his image and push up his approval rating, which stood at 25 percent in the latest IFOP poll, published on Sunday in the weekly Journal du Dimanche.

Chirac's rating was 30 percent in the IFOP survey, based on interviews conducted January 16-24 with 1,827 people of voting age. Both leaders' ratings have improved slightly in recent weeks from record lows in late 1996.
Chirac most recently ruled out a reshuffle in a December 12 television broadcast after persistent reports that Juppe was pressing for a cabinet shake-up.
